title: Docs: Console Optimization Suggestions (beta) — estimates, limitations, and safe rollout guidance
author: Elliot Price
release_notes:
- Adds a new Console doc page for Optimization Suggestions (beta)
- Adds explicit disclaimer language (estimates are not guarantees)
- Adds guidance on applying batching/caching changes safely using rollouts
- Adds troubleshooting section for empty states / insufficient telemetry / stale estimates
description:
Summary: This PR drafts the customer-facing docs for the Console > Optimize > Suggestions (beta) experience. The docs explain what Suggestions are (batching + caching only for beta), how Redwood calculates estimated savings and latency impact, how to interpret risk/confidence labels, and how to apply changes safely (rollouts + monitoring). Motivation: Support and early beta feedback flagged confusion around (a) what “risk” means, (b) why estimates can differ from billing, and (c) what steps are required to actually enable a recommendation. This doc aims to reduce back-and-forth during beta and set accurate expectations. Scope notes: This intentionally does NOT introduce quantization UI or promise contractual savings; it focuses on batching/caching recommendations surfaced in Console and the guardrails we expect customers to follow.

Key content included (high-level): 1) What you’ll see in Suggestions: list view metrics ($/day and %), latency deltas (p50/p95), and risk level (Low/Medium/High) with plain-language explanations. 2) How estimates work: inputs from aggregated telemetry (request rate, token counts, cache metrics, sequence length distribution), model pricing assumptions, and how we project savings and latency deltas; includes “stale as of” / recomputation cadence caveats. 3) What risk means: risk is performance/reliability/quality risk (not security risk); examples of what drives Medium/High. 4) Beta limitations: estimates can be wrong; confidence bands are conservative; no auto-apply; coverage depends on telemetry readiness and route eligibility. 5) How to apply safely: deep links to batching config + caching config; step-by-step rollout (canary first, monitor SLOs, rollback criteria), and what to watch in metrics. 6) Troubleshooting: common empty states (insufficient telemetry, not eligible, permissions), why billing may not match, and how to share feedback with Support.

Links: - Related backend/UI work: ENG-19358, ENG-19419 - Product scope and GA criteria: PM-842, PM-873 - Support context: SUP-48271, SUP-48315

conversation: Marissa Cole (review): The overall structure is good. Two asks: (1) please explicitly say risk is not a security classification, and (2) add a short paragraph that the estimate may differ from billing due to time windows + credits/discounts. Also, can we avoid the word “guarantee” except in the disclaimer section?

Elliot Price (author): Done. Added an explicit callout under Risk (“performance/reliability/quality only; not security risk”) and a Billing mismatch note in Troubleshooting. Also scrubbed a couple places where “guarantee” was used casually and replaced with “estimate”/“projection”.

Aditya Rao (review): Estimation section: can we clarify what’s included in ‘$/day’ (token spend only vs infra) and that we’re using observed token price for the current model/contract tier? Also would like the doc to avoid implying we simulate every prompt; it’s aggregate telemetry.

Elliot Price (author): Updated. ‘$/day’ now explicitly refers to estimated token spend for the specific route/model over the lookback window, based on observed request/token volumes and current pricing. Also clarified that we do not replay prompts; we use aggregates (token counts, latency distribution, cache metrics).

Tessa Morgan (design review): Copy tweak request: in the details drawer section, ‘Why we recommend this’ should be phrased as ‘Why you’re seeing this recommendation’ (less prescriptive). Also please align Low/Medium/High descriptions with the latest UI tooltip language (DES-640).
Elliot Price (author): Applied both changes. Pulled the tooltip language from the latest copy doc and updated the examples accordingly. Reworded the drawer section to match the UI.

Dev Patel (support readiness): Please add a ‘What we need from you’ bullet list for when customers report ‘estimate seems off’ (org, project, route, model, time window, screenshot including stale-as-of, whether they’re using caching already). This will cut cycles for SUP-48271-style tickets.

Elliot Price (author): Added a template under Troubleshooting > ‘If your estimate seems off’. Includes the exact fields Support asked for and a note on sharing screenshots without sensitive prompt content.

Dylan Brooks (eng review): Looks good. One small technical note: the recomputation cadence is “at least hourly” but can be delayed during pipeline backfill. Please add a sentence that the UI shows ‘stale as of’ and that delays can occur. Also confirm we’re not documenting any feature-flag steps (customer-facing).

Elliot Price (author): Updated staleness language to “computed periodically (typically hourly)”. Added that the UI surfaces ‘stale as of’ and that computation can lag. Confirmed we do not mention internal feature flags; access is described as “contact your Redwood team / request beta access”.
Marissa Cole (approval): Approved with the latest edits. Thanks for the explicit disclaimers and the apply-safely checklist; this should reduce confusion in beta.
